## Objective
- Build a complete, playable low-poly 3D battle royale game for mobile browsers, inspired by Free Fire, with touch controls, AI opponents, loot, combat, a shrinking zone, and match-end/restart flow.
- Validate the game in-browser and fix any discovered issues.

## Requirements
- Include third-person movement and camera, mobile HUD and touch controls, varied island terrain and structures, three weapon classes, loot, 15–20 AI opponents, a shrinking danger zone, audio feedback, and victory/defeat screens.
- Save and inspect a small JPEG screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a standalone `index.html` using Three.js from jsDelivr CDN.
- Used a deterministic low-poly island and 17 AI opponents; support both mobile and desktop controls.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the game prototype with terrain, structures, player and bots, weapons, loot, zone phases, HUD, minimap, audio cues, and match-end/restart UI.
- Extracted the inline module and ran `node --check`; no syntax errors.
- Started a local server with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- Opened the page with `playwright-cli`; title is `LAST LIGHT — Battle Royale`.
- Captured and inspected `screenshots/last-light-menu.jpg`.

### Active
- Validate an active match in-browser: movement, aiming, firing, loot pickup, zone, and restart.
- Fix any visual or gameplay defects found during testing.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Click `DEPLOY TO ISLAND` and inspect the active match screenshot and console.
2. Test movement, aiming, firing, loot pickup, and restart; address any defects.
3. Report completed features, validation performed, and any remaining assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation, styling, Three.js scene, AI, gameplay, and controls.
- `screenshots/last-light-menu.jpg`: Latest captured and inspected menu screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Browser console showed one 404 for `/favicon.ico` and WebGL GPU-stall performance warnings; no game errors were reported.
- A potential issue to investigate: verify player movement coordinates and camera behavior during play.
